Nonlinear posterior sampling from sparse moving-camera images

A mixture of preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (optionally gradient-guided pCNL), independent, and component-transport Metropolis transitions uses the full nonlinear observed-image likelihood. A local Gaussian mixture preconditions the proposals. Warmup is discarded and adaptation stops before retained draws. Ground truth is used only after sampling for evaluation.

Read convergence before prediction scores. Every latent coordinate, observed log likelihood, and adaptive process scale is monitored using rank-normalized/folded split Rhat and bulk/tail ESS. Rhat must be below 1.01, both ESS at least 400, and no chain frozen. Failed checks mean the displayed intervals remain provisional. Passing checks cannot exclude unseen modes or establish physical calibration.

Prediction scores use an equal, evenly spaced rendering subset per chain to control memory. All retained states enter the diagnostics. Correlated states are not independent experiments. The cases use one known geometry and camera path.
